articles.title: Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability
articles.summary: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

image.caption: The French government is facing protests over the rising cost of living, and is also grappling with mounting debt costsImage: Reuters

blocks.text: Deeply indebted, politically trapped in a standoff between extremes and led by a government without a parliamentary majority: These are the defining features of France's current predicament.

If, in response to nationwide protests, the government plans to provide €4 billion ($4.48 billion) in low-interest loans to renovate schools by 2030 and allocate a further €1 billion to universities by 2029, it is promising money the state simply does not have.

France's public debt stands at around 120% of gross domestic product (GDP). By comparison, Germany's debt-to-GDP ratio is roughly 65%, despite its €600 billion investment package for infrastructure and defense.

Germany still enjoys the highest possible AAA credit rating. France, by contrast, is rated AA, A+ or Aa3, depending on the credit agency. While Germany's outlook is consistently rated as stable, several agencies have assigned France a negative outlook.

As a result, the French government must pay higher interest rates on its borrowing than Berlin. The risk premium over German government bonds, known as the spread, is now at its highest level since the financial crisis. France pays nearly 1.6 percentage points more in interest than Germany on 10-year bonds.
A barometer of France's public finances
The spread acts as a kind of "fever gauge" for bond markets, explained Friedrich Heinemann, an economist at the Leibniz Center for European Economic Research (ZEW) in Mannheim.

"This fever gauge then forces a change of course. If the spread rises too sharply, France's financing conditions come under pressure, and anyone in France who needs a loan has to pay higher interest rates. Banks then get into trouble, and the crisis escalates further," Heinemann told DW.

"This could then slide toward a financial crisis, which would finally send a clear signal to everyone: Things cannot continue like this unless you are prepared to risk a genuine economic collapse," he said.

Landry Charrier, a researcher at the University of Bonn's Center for Advanced Security, Strategic and Integration Studies, however, does not expect France's debt-fueled spending spree to end anytime soon.

"French people are aware of the country's high public debt. But debt remains an abstract concept if its consequences are barely felt in everyday life. According to INSEE [the French national statistics agency — Editor's note], 56% of the population receive more in government benefits and services than they pay in taxes and social contributions. The majority therefore have a tangible interest in maintaining the status quo," Charrier told DW.
For more than half a century, France has regularly spent more than it collects in tax revenue. The last time it balanced its national budget was in 1974.
Echoes of eurozone crisis

France last paid a similarly high-risk premium at the end of 2011, during the eurozone debt crisis. What is particularly striking is how quickly it has risen: Since June 2026, the spread over German government bonds has more than doubled.

The main driver is not so much the general level of interest rates. Rather, it's the growing risk premium investors demand in response to high debt levels, political instability, large budget deficits and the recent unrest.

The higher the interest rates, the larger the share of the national budget that must be devoted to debt servicing alone. France is expected to pay more than €79 billion in interest on its total public debt in 2026. That figure is projected to exceed €91 billion in 2027 and could reach between €125 billion and €132 billion by 2030.

These figures include the costs incurred by social security funds and local authorities. The central government's interest bill alone is currently estimated at €62.6 billion by the Agence France Tresor, a French Treasury agency.

In the coming years, France will have to refinance large amounts of outstanding bonds that were issued when interest rates were at historic lows. At the same time, the country's substantial budget deficit means it must take on additional debt.
Warning shot for Germany
The trend of rising interest costs is also affecting Germany. The ZEW's Heinemann has calculated that German interest payments are likely to increase sharply by the early 2030s.

"For the federal government alone, which has so far paid around €30 billion, the figure will triple within a few years as both debt and interest rates rise. And it won't stop there — it will exceed €90 billion. Reaching €100 billion in annual interest payments in the federal budget is then no longer far off," warned the economist.
Could France's debt crisis become a problem for Europe?
In France, however, economic realities seem to have little impact on political debate. Both the far-right National Rally (RN) and the far-left France Unbowed (LFI) are campaigning on costly promises.

RN leader Marine Le Pen, for example, wants to reinstate the retirement age of 62 while promising €140 billion in savings. Jean-Luc Melenchon, LFI's leader, has even suggested that government bonds held by the French central bank should be "thrown into the fire."
"Nobody will ever notice they've disappeared," he has claimed.
'Fairy tales from the left and the right'
For Heinemann, this is "a good example of radical parties on both the right and the left simply telling economic fairy tales."
Their common message, he said, is that "there is a way out of this mess that requires neither fiscal consolidation nor painful cuts."
Charrier is convinced that many French people have yet to grasp the seriousness of the situation.
"The euro has made it easier for France to access cheap financing and has long softened the pressure to adjust," he pointed out.

"In the past, currency devaluations [of the French franc — Editor's note] made economic imbalances immediately felt through declining purchasing power and rising prices. Today, that warning signal is missing. This has created the illusion that necessary adjustments can be postponed indefinitely," Charrier said.
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: Texas mayor instructs police to limit co-operation with ICE
articles.summary: There has been months of public outcry in Houston after an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer fatally shot a man who was driving to work.

blocks.text: The mayor of Houston, Texas, has directed the city's police to limit co-operation with federal immigration officials.

The move by John Whitmire, a Democrat, comes on the heels of stunning victories by the party in Texas during this week's midterm elections. It breaks with policy set by Republican Governor Greg Abbott, who lost his re-election bid.
"I do this to begin a healing process," Whitmire said on Friday, and to "reduce fear and anxiety across our community". He added: "I also do this knowing that elections matter."
There has been months of public outcry in Houston after an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer fatally shot a man who was driving to work.

Houston police chief Noe Diaz said on Friday that officers will now only contact ICE if someone they arrest for a jailable offence also has an administrative ICE warrant, which are issued internally by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), within which ICE operates.
"For example, if our police officers pull someone over for a minor traffic infraction and they write a citation, that person receives a citation and goes about their day," Diaz said.

Under the previous rules, Houston police officers were required to inform ICE if anyone they were dealing with came up as having one of these warrants attached to their name when they were searched on the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) - a digital database that includes records on wanted persons, stolen property, certain missing people and those arrested and fingerprinted for serious offences.
Whitmire said on Friday that he had directed the Houston Police Department to make the changes through an executive order.
He also called on Congress to change federal immigration rules, saying "ICE needs better training. They need body cameras. They need to be trained in de-escalation."
He added, "But this can only be done in Washington. I can only control what I can control."

In response, a spokesperson for the DHS told Houston's NBC affiliate, KPRC 2, in a statement: "We remain disappointed that sanctuary politicians seek to limit cooperation with ICE, as our law enforcement are simply fulfilling their sworn duties to serve and protect our communities."
"Partnerships with law enforcement are critical to having the resources we need to arrest criminal illegal aliens across the country," the spokesperson added.
Another Texas city, Austin, has also begun implementing a similar policy change.
Democrats won both the US Senate and House of Representatives in Tuesday's midterms, taking control of Congress for the rest of Donald Trump's presidency.

Texas, a long-time Republican stronghold, was the site of one of the most stunning upsets in the vote, with the state electing its first Latina governor, Gina Hinojosa, as the first Democrat governor since 1995. It also elected its first Democratic senator since 1988.
Whitmire has previously faced criticism for abiding by immigration enforcement policies under the Trump administration.
He had resisted previous calls to implement similar changes over concerns that the White House could send a surge of immigration officials in response. , external
Abbott has also threatened to take pull millions in funds from cities like Houston, Dallas and Austin unless they allow police to cooperate fully with federal immigration officials.
The BBC has contacted Abbott's office for comment.
Whitmire's announcement comes a week after an ICE officer was charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon after he allegedly hit a man with a vehicle in Texas.
Earlier this year, large protests broke out in Houston after an ICE officer fatally shot a man driving to work.
The deceased, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a 52-year-old Mexican national who lived in the US as an undocumented immigrant for decades, was not the intended target, officials said after the incident.

articles.summary: ‘I won't let this title be taken away because I am the only world champion of the Philippines now,’ says Pedro Taduran, the pride of Libon, Albay who looks to defend his IBF minimumweight crown

blocks.text: FACE-OFF. Filipino champion Pedro Taduran and Brandon Romero of Spain during the weigh-in ahead of their IBF minimumweight bout.
SALITA PROMOTIONS
‘I won't let this title be taken away because I am the only world champion of the Philippines now,’ says Pedro Taduran, the pride of Libon, Albay who looks to defend his IBF minimumweight crown
MANILA, Philippines – Pedro Taduran is the last champion standing in Philippine boxing.

He promised that it would stay that way after his fourth defense of the IBF (International Boxing Federation) minimumweight crown against Spaniard Brandon Romero on Saturday, November 7 (Sunday, November 8, Philippine time) at the Kiva Auditorium in Albuquerque, New Mexico, USA.

“I won’t let this title be taken away because I am the only world champion of the Philippines now. I’ll fight for it to the best of my abilities,” Taduran said in Filipino during the pre-fight press conference on Friday, November 6.
Bookmakers believe the pride of Libon, Albay, would succeed in his noble mission.
The 30-year-old Taduran, owner of a 20-win (14 knockouts), 4-loss, 1-draw record, is the heavy favorite. With an 87 percent chance of winning and staining Moreno’s clean 16-0 slate with 5 knockouts.
Moreno admits he holds Taduran in high esteem, but thinks his movement and ability to adjust during fights will be key to his dream to win a world crown in the United States.

Taduran spent the early part of his preparations at the Elorde Sports Center in Sucat, Paranaque, before finishing his training at the Knuckleheads Boxing Gym of MP Promotions president Sean Gibbons in Las Vegas, Nevada.
Former world junior bantamweight king Jerwin Ancajas and his longtime trainer/manager Joven Jimenez supervised Taduran’s training in the United States.
“He has made weight and is ready to fight,” Jimenez told Rappler hours before the official weigh-in.
True enough, Taduran checked in at 104,8 pounds, while Romero tipped the scales at an exact 105.
Taduran became the lone Filipino world champion after Melvin Jerusalem yielded the WBC (World Boxing Council) minimumweight belt to Siyakholwa Kuse on May 16 in South Africa. – Rappler.com

articles.title: US: Giant pandas from China make public debut at Atlanta zoo
articles.summary: Ping Ping and Fu Shuang are the first giant pandas to be housed in Zoo Atlanta after a gap of two years.

image.caption: Ping Ping has distinctive dark circles surrounding his eyesImage: Elijah Nouvelage/AFP

blocks.text: Two giant pandas from China have made their first public appearance at a zoo in the US city of Atlanta as a queue of visitors lined up to see the bears.
In a treat for them and their fans, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang — male and female, respectively — were seen munching on bamboo at Zoo Atlanta on Friday.
The six-year-old pandas arrived from China's Chengdu on September 27.
The FedEx flight they traveled on was dubbed the "Panda Express."
The panda duo had spent the last few weeks getting acclimated to their habitat.
Pandas return to Atlanta
Ping Ping and Fu Shuang have taken up residence in a panda enclosure at the zoo that had been vacant since 2024.

A 25-year-long partnership that saw Atlanta host four pandas on loan since 1999 ended in the midst of strained US-China ties. Seven panda cubs that were born at the zoo during that period now live in Chengdu, China.
That arrangement has been renewed under a 10-year loan agreement following a Washington summit between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping.
China's ambassador to the US, Xie Feng, said at a press conference on Friday that the pandas' arrival "marks the renewal of a decade-long bond between China and Zoo Atlanta."

blocks.caption: Fu Shuang, the female, has a protruding foreheadImage: Brynn Anderson/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Raymond King, CEO of Zoo Atlanta, described pandas as "animals that have got a unique ability to inspire curiosity, instill passion, evoke joy, and unite people around the globe."
"This extraordinary spirit of partnership helps create a future for a species that is truly beloved the world over," he said as the two adult pandas made their debut.
China's 'panda diplomacy'
China has a history of leasing the iconic pandas to other countries in a bid to build diplomatic ties, dubbed "panda diplomacy."
Cubs born in foreign zoos are typically sent back to China.

blocks.caption: Fu Shuang sits in her enclosureImage: Elijah Nouvelage/AFP

blocks.text: Meanwhile, unaware of the soft power they wield, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, lounged about their new habitat on Friday.
The zoo recently renovated its panda facilities and has also ensured a long-term supply of locally grown bamboo for its newest residents.
Three US zoos now house the black-and-white mammals.

articles.title: Meghan's father Thomas Markle under house arrest after child sex abuse material charge
articles.summary: The 82-year-old appeared in court in Florida after the FBI searched two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented.

blocks.text: Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, has been placed under house detention at his assisted living facility in Florida after being charged over possession of child sex abuse material.
Markle, 82, was arrested in Florida on a federal complaint alleging he held images that show child sex abuse, the US Department of Justice (DoJ) said.
He is charged with one count of possessing indecent images of children, the DoJ said. Markle has previously denied allegations of possessing images of child sex abuse, calling them "sick lies".
In a 30-minute court hearing on Friday he was also ordered to submit to electronic monitoring, but no plea was taken.
At the court hearing, the charges were laid out against him by federal prosecutor Courtenay Derry, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News.
He was brought into court in a wheelchair, escorted by two US Marshals. Markle was wearing black trousers and a black t-shirt.
No plea was taken during the hearing, and an arraignment date in California will be determined in due course, a joint statement from the DoJ and the US Attorney's Office Central California said.
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have not commented on Markle's arrest.

Markle was arrested after the FBI, acting on warrants, searched storage units in LA registered to him which he had rented since 2008, with the last payment being made in October this year, the DoJ said.
Inside the units the FBI says agents seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained child sex abuse material.
FBI director Kash Patel said authorities "moved quickly" when arresting Markle.
"Mr Markle allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions," Patel said.

He added that the FBI would "use every single resource at our disposal to protect innocent kids – any predator who targets children will have zero safe haven in this country or anywhere they try to hide".
Witnesses "positively identified" Markle in two of the images believed to contain child sex abuse material.
In those images, the man pictured "appears to be in the age range of 30s to 40s", which suggests the alleged abuse dates back decades as Markle is currently 82 years old.
Last month, police in the Philippines obtained a warrant to examine devices allegedly removed from Markle's former home in the country.
Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old video tapes, were handed to officers by Meghan's half brother Thomas Markle Jr.

Markle Sr moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes, and lived in Cebu until May. He was then reportedly living in a Florida rehabilitation centre learning to walk again after having his leg amputated.
In October, London's Metropolitan Police confirmed that it had received a letter in 2019 making a "number of claims" relating to Markle Sr.

The Met said information contained in the letter, which related to allegations against Meghan's father outside the UK, was passed on to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, but it did not share it with other law enforcement agencies.
The force has since voluntarily referred itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IPOC) over its handling of the letter.

In a statement released in October after the allegations against Markle Sr emerged, the Duchess of Sussex said: "I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."
Meghan has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year.

blocks.text: What you need to know

items: India's Supreme Court reviews Delhi's approach to tackling air pollution
Air quality in the capital has plummeted again as winter nears
Pollution also regularly spikes during Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights, which sees huge amounts of fireworks set off
Social media giant X says orders asking for the removal of free speech groups in India were fake

blocks.text: Here's a roundup of headlines from across India on Saturday, November 7:
November 7, 2026
India's top court says vehicle emissions a main cause of Delhi's low air quality

blocks.caption: Delhi authorities have urged people to avoid or limit outdoor activitiesImage: Bhawika Chhabra/REUTERS

blocks.text: The Supreme Court of India on Friday said that vehicular pollution is a major contributor to the deteriorating air quality in Delhi and questioned the effectiveness of the government's measures to curb it.
The bench, comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, opened the proceedings with a jibe saying, "I hope you all are enjoying the weather in Delhi."
This week, Delhi's Air Quality Index (AQI) has remained above the "hazardous" 300 mark.
Air quality in the capital regularly plummets at the outset of winter, as weather conditions help trap pollutants.

"A major cause of the pollution is vehicular pollution. Look at the roads in Delhi, look at the roads connecting Delhi to the NCR (the National Capital Region)… the kind of bumper-to-bumper traffic… that's the major cause," the CJI said.
The court examined the steps taken by the government to control the rising levels of air pollution.

Expressing concerns over the failure of measures to curb air pollution in Delhi over the years, the court said, "To think we can achieve air quality of less than 100 AQI in Delhi during winters is utopian when 'very poor' and 'severe' have become the new normal."
On stubble burning, the court said farmers should be given economic incentives and practical alternatives.
The court also encouraged responsible celebrations during festivals, particularly Diwali, where firecrackers being set off adds to the air pollution.
"Why don't we revert to our original customs?" the CJI said, adding celebrations should be accompanied by a sense of responsibility towards the environment.
India's worst air pollution crisis isn't in its megacities

articles.title: BI supports DOTr push for wider e-gates in NAIA
articles.summary: The Bureau of Immigration (BI) supported the Department of Transportation"s (DOTr) proposal to expand the use of electronic immigration gates (e-gates) across Ninoy Aquino International Airport…

blocks.text: Published November 7, 2026 3:00pm

The Bureau of Immigration (BI) supported the Department of Transportation’s (DOTr) proposal to expand the use of electronic immigration gates (e-gates) across Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) to speed up passenger clearance and reduce the necessity of immigration interviews.
DOTr Secretary Vince Dizon previously said that he is eyeing recommending the wider use of e-gates, allowing them to be utilized by all passengers departing from and arriving in the Philippines.

BI Commissioner Joel Anthony Viado said this proposal aligns with the bureau's modernization agenda and efforts to reduce queues, speed up passenger processing, and strengthen border security, while fulfilling its mandate to combat human trafficking and other cross-border crimes.

E-gates enable passengers who have been cleared by automated screening to skip routine face-to-face immigration interviews. Therefore, only those flagged by the system or requiring further assessment will be subjected to examination by immigration officers.
At present, only outbound foreigners and Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) are allowed to use the e-gates, requiring other departing Filipinos to still undergo immigration interviews.
Meanwhile, for arriving passengers, only Filipinos are currently allowed to use the e-gates.
“Technology should allow us to process legitimate travelers faster while enabling our officers to focus on passengers who require closer scrutiny,” Viado said.

“Wider e-Gate access must go hand in hand with reliable biometric verification and effective security checks. Our objective is not only to reduce queues but also to make immigration screening faster, smarter, and more secure,” he added.
The bureau said it has been expanding and upgrading e-gates in international airports outside Metro Manila, with the first phase already completed in Clark, Cebu, and Davao.

An added security feature at the gates is the Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS), a software that enhances biometric identification and verification capabilities to detect multiple-passport holders and other fraudulent activity.

The bureau said the integration of ABIS into e-gates will help authorities to identify passengers who may pose immigration or security risks while also ensuring faster clearance for legitimate travelers.
Procurement is still ongoing for the second phase of the program, which will cover other provincial international ports.
A livestreamed bidding will likewise be implemented, similar to the first phase, according to the BI. --VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz could reopen as part of Qatari plan for Iran nuclear inspections
articles.summary:
Trump still considering new assault on Iran nuclear sites – though threats less credible after Vance remarks

Qatar, the lead mediator in the US-Iran conflict, is seeking to persuade Tehran…

blocks.text: Qatar, the lead mediator in the US-Iran conflict, is seeking to persuade Tehran to allow UN nuclear weapons inspectors to visit Iran’s bombed nuclear sites, including those housing the country’s stockpile of highly enriched uranium.
Iran would not be required to make any commitment that the stockpile would be removed from the country, with other options on the table, including reducing the uranium content by down-blending it.
Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani, the emir of Qatar, spoke to Donald Trump about the proposal, the emir’s office said on Friday without revealing the call’s contents.
The state news agency said the emir “emphasised the importance of continuing dialogue and embracing diplomacy as a means of resolving disputes, preventing further escalation in the region”.

Trump is still considering whether to mount a further assault on Iranian nuclear sites, though the credibility of his threats is weaker inside Iran after his vice-president, JD Vance, said the war itself, and not just its cost to American consumers, was critical to the collapse of the Republican vote in the US midterms.

Under the Qatar proposal, the US would immediately lift the naval blockade on Iran in the strait of Hormuz and release a portion of the $8bn (£6bn) of its frozen assets. In return, Iran would agree to visits by International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors to its bombed nuclear facilities, based on a previous abandoned agreement that had been reached in Cairo in September 2025.
Iran would open the strait of Hormuz on the second day, via a route it has already negotiated with Oman that they would jointly lodge with the International Maritime Organisation (IMO).

Iran has multiple other preconditions for opening the strait including ending the war in Lebanon, a withdrawal of US forces from the Iranian coastline, a commitment to lift some economic sanctions, and agreement to pay war reparations. The sequencing of these commitments has been at the heart of the mediation.
In the memorandum of understanding, a $300bn reconstruction and development fund was to be set up to help Iran recover economically, but it was never clear exactly how this proposal was to be funded.

Iran, in a triumphalist mood after Trump’s election wipeout, has been wary of allowing the UN nuclear inspectors back into the country, claiming it had lost faith in Rafael Grossi, the head of the inspectorate.

blocks.caption: A billboard bearing the message ‘we will kill Trump’ in Tehran. Photograph: Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Tehran claims Grossi betrayed his duty to uphold the nuclear non-proliferation treaty, by failing to criticise the US for bombing Iran’s nuclear sites. It fears that material gathered by the inspectors would be handed over as targeting data to the Americans and Israelis.

In the parallel talks on opening the strait, Oman’s foreign minister, Badr Albusaidi, spoke again to Iran about the future of the strait administration including the agreed route, the extent to which the agreement is temporary and the need to register the proposal with the IMO, either as a bilateral agreement or a joint regional proposal.
Oman has a long-term proposal for the administration of the strait compliant with the law of the sea in that shipping companies would be charged only for services, and not tolls.

Amir Hayat Moqaddam, the deputy chair of the Iranian parliament’s national security and foreign policy committee, told the Iranian Students’ News Agency (ISNA) on Tuesday that ships from four countries – China, India, Qatar and Iraq – were allowed to pass through the strategic waterway.

The exemptions served mutual interests, he said, adding that Iran charged Indian and Chinese vessels transit fees while allowing Qatari ships to pass free of charge. Medicine was received from India, while China provided political support.

It is reported that of the 10.23m barrels a day of Gulf crude that passed through the strait in October, about 42% went to China and 13% to India, said Muyu Xu, a senior crude oil analyst at the analytics firm Kpler.

The navy of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said two “violating” oil tankers attempting to pass through an unauthorised route in the eastern sector of the strait of Hormuz had collided with mines and caught fire.
The IRGC said the two tankers had turned off their navigation and identification systems and that the attempted crossing was with the support of US military forces.

articles.title: Harvesting 30 years of music: Gloc-9 brings ‘Mga Ani’ to vinyl
articles.summary: Gloc-9 drops 11 of his most impactful songs in his first vinyl release, sharing some advice for young artists on mastering their craft

items: Filipino hip-hop artist Gloc-9 celebrates nearly 30 years in the music industry with his first vinyl release, 'Mga Ani ni Gloc-9', featuring 11 iconic tracks that reflect his storytelling and social commentary.

The collection includes collaborations with various artists and emphasizes the importance of continuous effort in the music industry, as Gloc-9 shares his thoughts on the meaning of his songs evolving over time.
Gloc-9 encourages the youth to identify their gifts and pursue their passions with authenticity, believing that true happiness in one's craft will lead to success, regardless of trends.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Filipino hip-hop pillar Gloc-9 marks nearly three decades in the music industry with Mga Ani ni Gloc-9, his first vinyl release. The limited-edition collection features 11 of his most iconic storytelling tracks from different record labels.
From his greatest hits to hard-hitting commentaries, the record serves as a compilation of the social realities and personal struggles that define his musical legacy.

“Kaya ‘Ani ni Gloc-9’ ang ipinangalan namin dahil feeling ko, sa almost 30 years ko in the industry, I just hope na halos lahat ng mga songs na ginawa ko, somehow buhatin ako kung gaano ko pa katagal puwedeng gawin ito,” he said.

(That’s why we named it ‘Ani ni Gloc-9’ [Gloc-9’s Harvest], I feel that, after nearly 30 years in the industry, I just hope that the songs I’ve created will, in some way, carry me forward for as long as I’m able to keep doing this.)
Some of the songs in the vinyl collection are“Sirena” featuring Ebe Dancel, “Magda” featuring Rico Blanco, and “Upuan” featuring Jeazell Grutas.

Other included tracks: “Simpleng Tao”and “Bagsakan,” which he recorded with Parokya ni Edgar and the late master rapper Francis M. Also part of the list are songs like “Love Story,” “Walang Natira” featuring Sheng Belmonte, “Lando” featuring Francis M, “Takipsilim” featuring Regine Velasquez-Alcasid, “Walang Pumapalakpak” featuring Gary Valenciano, and“Kumpisal”featuring Skusta Clee.
The title of the collection, Mga Ani ni Gloc-9, also pertains to what Gloc-9 has reaped in all his years in OPM.

“Ganoon naman talaga, lalo na sa industriya na ito,” he said during the launch. “Mas madami kang itinanim, mas madami kang aanihin. Hindi naman lahat ng ani mo, ay [may makukuha] ka. Kailangan mo siyang ulitin nang ulitin.”

(That’s just how it is, especially in this industry. The more you plant, the more you harvest. But you don’t necessarily get to keep everything you harvest. You have to keep doing it over and over again.)

For Gloc-9, something that can be said to be his ani or harvest, are the moments when he’s at events while singing, and he also hears people singing his songs, to the point that he doesn’t even need to sing in the first place.
“Honest, iyon yung mga moments na gusto kong maiyak,” he shared. “Siguro enough na yung nilagay kong pagtatanim sa tagal ng panahon. Baka sakali puwede na kong umani.”
(Honestly, those are the moments when I want to cry. Perhaps the seeds I’ve sown over all this time are enough. Maybe it’s time for me to reap the harvest.)
In his many years in the business, Gloc-9 has said he hopes to collaborate with Popstar Royalty Sarah Geronimo in the future.
Gloc-9 shared that the songs he chose for this milestone — the vinyl collection came out under Sony Music Philippines, Star Music, and Universal Records — are not necessarily his greatest hits.
“Hindi yung hits siguro, pero kung ano yung may pinaka may nakalabit na mga songs, kaya namin nilagay diyan,” he said.
(Maybe not necessarily the hits, but we included the songs with the greatest impact, which is why we put those in the vinyl collection.)
He also said among the songs in the collection, the award-winning “Upuan” has taken on a completely different meaning for him over time.
Written 17 years ago when Gloc-9 was 33, the track reflects a time when he admits he was still naive and hopeful.

“Naririnig ko na kapag kinakanta ko siya sa harap ng ibang tao, alam ko kung ano ang intentions ko,” he said. “Pero may times na naririnig ko siya sa iba’t-ibang lugar na alam ko din na hindi na iyon ang intensyon ko sa kanta. Napalitan na.”
(When I sing that song in front of others, I know my intentions. But there are times when I hear it in various places, and I know that’s no longer the intention I had for the song. It has changed.)
Gloc-9 has always been known for commenting about current issues through his music. Again, he cites “Upuan” as the song from his vinyl collection that should resonate the most with the youth today.

“Siguro dahil sa mga nangyayari ngayon,” he explained to Rappler. “Siguro magtuturo iyon ng awareness sa kanila. Maging matapang sila. Naniniwala kasi ako na hindi dahil ako yung gumawa ng song, ako iyong kumanta nung song, ako lang ang kakanta noon. Ito ay ginawa namin, para kantahin iyon. Maging boses din nila.”

(Maybe it’s because of the things happening nowadays. The song should teach awareness to the youth. I hope it makes them brave. I believe that just because I wrote the song and sang it, it doesn’t mean I’m the only one who should sing it. We created this so that others could sing it, too. It could become their voice as well.)
Gloc-9 also shared his advice to anyone who might want to follow in his footsteps.

“Napaka-simple lang, noh,” said Gloc-9. “I think ang dapat magawa ng kabataan ngayon ay whatever it is na gusto nila i-pursue sa buhay nila, is to identify kung ano yung gifts nila. Kung ano yung specific na gift nila. I think iyon ang pinaka-importante. Kapag nakita mo siya, na-identify mo siya, the earlier the better. Tapos after that, you build. You build, you build, you build.”

(It’s really simple. I think what young people today should do, regardless of what they want to pursue in life, is to identify their gifts. They need to figure out what their specific gift is. I believe that is the most important thing. Once you discover or identify it, and the earlier, the better, then you build. You just keep building.)

“Kung saan ka masaya na ginagawa mo ‘yun, regardless of anything,” he added. “Pera, oras, opportunity, kung anong katayuan mo sa buhay. Kung lahat nang iyon, ‘di mo papansinin, tapos masaya ka sa ginagawa mo, iyon ang i-build mo, tuloy-tuloy. Eventually, may mangyayari. Imposibleng wala.”

(Your calling should be what makes you happy. You do it anyway regardless of money, time, opportunity, or whatever your circumstances in life. If you’re happy with what you do, build on that. Eventually something will happen — it’s impossible that nothing will happen.)
He gave more advice for those who also want to get into the music industry.
“Kahit ‘di ikaw yung uso, kung ang craft mo iyong ginawa mo with purity and good intentions, hindi mo kailangan maging uso,” he shared. “Laging merong makikinig sa iyo.”

(Even if your music is not the trend or the current rage, if you do your craft with purity and good intentions, you don’t need to be trendy. There will always be someone who will listen to you.) – Rappler.com

articles.title: Pope in 'pretty good health' as he starts Latin America tour
articles.summary: Pope Leo travels to Uruguay just three weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.

blocks.text: Pope Leo XIV has told reporters travelling with him to Latin America he is "in pretty good health", in his first comments on his condition since having surgery for lung cancer.
The Pope has arrived in Uruguay, the first stop of a 12-day tour which he is undertaking only three weeks after his operation.
The pontiff, 71, also said he was "very happy" to be able to make the trip which was thrown into doubt last month when doctors discovered a tumour during a routine scan.
The tour will cover Argentina and a much anticipated return to Peru, which the Vatican described as a "homecoming" as the Pope was based there for many years as a missionary, then a bishop.
"I must confess that, from the very first day, I never had any doubts; I was convinced that this journey had to go forward," the Pope told journalists on his plane to Uruguay.
"Thanks to the marvellous medical staff... I believe I am in quite good health," Pope Leo confirmed.
Last month's operation to remove a tumour was successful and his doctors say the cancer has not spread.
On Friday, he arrived in Monetevideo to a seafront lined with crowds shouting his name as his Popemobile passed.
In his first speech of the trip, the Pope said universal healthcare should be "accessible to everyone".
He told the crowd in Plaza Independencia the care he received made him think of the "many men and women who lack the means to obtain a timely diagnosis" or receive treatment.
He capped his day with a prayer at the Montevideo Cathedral.
Pope Leo will cover more than 20,000 miles on his sixth international tour.
On Sunday he will travel to Argentina, the homeland of his predecessor Pope Francis who did not return during his own papacy.
The Pope said his visit was about being near the people who were looking to the Church for a message of "hope".

articles.title: MIAA turns over operational control of CCTV cameras to NNIC
articles.summary: The Manila International Airport Authority (MIAA) has turned over the operational control of more than 2,100 closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA)…

blocks.text: Published November 7, 2026 2:37pm

The Manila International Airport Authority (MIAA) has turned over the operational control of more than 2,100 closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) to the New NAIA Infra Corp. (NNIC).

In a statement on Saturday, the MIAA said the transfer of CCTV operational control is part of the transition of NAIA's operations and maintenance responsibilities to NNIC as the gateway's private concessionaire, pursuant to the NAIA Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Concession Agreement.

Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon, who had lost his cool over the alleged lengthy transfer process, witnessed the turnover held Friday. He was joined by MIAA Senior Assistant General Manager Ma. Lourdes Reyes, and NNIC Executive Assistant to the President and CEO Cesar Chiong.

Meanwhile, the MIAA said it continues to perform its regulatory and oversight functions, ensuring NNIC's compliance with the terms of the concession agreement, together with applicable performance standards and service quality requirements.

"MIAA remains committed to working closely with DOTr, NNIC, and other airport stakeholders to ensure the continued safety and security of passengers, airport personnel, and other airport users," it said.
Previously, the MIAA promised to complete the turnover of the CCTV surveillance system to the NAIA's private management by November 2026.

This came promptly after Dizon lashed out at airport officials for failing to turn over the security camera system to the NNIC. Dizon gave the officials until November to complete the turnover before people start getting fired.

Dizon reprimanded the airport officials for failing to take responsibility over the CCTV matter after a theft was reported, especially since he already ordered the turnover a year ago during his first stint as secretary of the Department of Transportation (DOTr).

Dizon was then appointed into the Department of Public Works and Highways, with Giovanni Lopez replacing him as Transport Secretary. Dizon and Lopez swapped Cabinet posts last Monday, with the former assuming the helm at the DOTr once more. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: China thanks Philippines for help in repatriating over 100 POGO-linked suspects
articles.summary: The Chinese Embassy in the Philippines has thanked Philippine law enforcement authorities for helping repatriate more than 100 Chinese nationals suspected of involvement in gambling and fraud.

blocks.text: November 7, 2026 | 2:33pm

Chinese nationals suspected of involvement in illegal Philippine offshore gaming operations (POGOs) are repatriated to China following a joint operation by Philippine and Chinese law enforcement authorities on Nov. 6, 2026.
Chinese Embassy Manila via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — The Chinese Embassy in the Philippines has thanked Philippine law enforcement authorities for helping repatriate more than 100 Chinese nationals suspected of involvement in gambling and fraud.
In a Facebook post on Saturday, November 7, the embassy said the two countries jointly repatriated the suspects on Friday, November 6.
"China appreciates the assistance provided by relevant Philippine law enforcement authorities," it said.
The embassy described the operation as "another major achievement" in the two countries' efforts to combat transnational crime.
Since 2023, cooperation between Chinese and Philippine authorities has resulted in the repatriation of more than 2,600 suspects, the embassy said.
"China's resolve to combat transnational crimes, including gambling and fraud, remains unwavering," it added.

The embassy also said it was ready to continue working closely with Philippine authorities and take "all necessary measures" to safeguard personnel exchanges and economic and trade cooperation between the two countries.

The latest repatriation comes amid the government's crackdown on Philippine offshore gaming operators (POGOs), following President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s announcement of a nationwide ban on the industry during his third State of the Nation Address in July 2024.
POGOs were companies licensed to offer online gambling services to offshore customers, many of whom were based in China, where gambling is prohibited.
While the industry generated revenue and employment, some POGO hubs were linked to criminal activities, including human trafficking, kidnapping, money laundering and online scams.
Marcos later signed Executive Order No. 74, directing all licensed POGOs and related offshore gaming operations to cease operations by Dec. 31, 2024.
Despite the ban, Philippine authorities have continued to conduct raids against illegal offshore gaming operations.

articles.title: Ombudsman calls out BJMP for allowing Romualdez aid while in detention

Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla called out the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) for allowing former House speaker Martin Romualdez to have a personal assistant while incarcerated.
Speaking on his program at DZRH, Remulla doubled down on earlier comments regarding Romualdez’s supposed aide.
“Nagugulat ako eh.. Walang dahilan yan para payagan yan. Ano yan? Mayroong nakakulong na mayaman na may alalay? Na galing sa labas? Ano yan? Mafia?," Remulla said on his radio program on Saturday.
(I was shocked… There is no reason to allow that. What is that? A detained person that has an aide? That came from outside?)
“Imbestigahan ko yan. Imibistigahan ko yan,” Remulla added.
(I will investigate that, I will investigate that.)
Remulla said he knew the people behind it, but would not mention their names.
The BJMP has since responded to Remulla, saying that they respect his comments and would also investigate the matter.

“The Bureau is conducting an investigation into the arrangement authorized by one of its jail wardens. Pursuant to the directive of the DILG (Department of Interior and Local Government) Secretary, the BJMP will submit its comprehensive report to the Department within the prescribed period,” the Bureau said in a statement.

“The BJMP will not tolerate unauthorized privileges or any form of preferential treatment in the custody of persons deprived of liberty. Should any violation of policies be established, appropriate action will be taken against the personnel found responsible,” it added. --VAL, GMA News

articles.title: NZ election 2026 live results: count on as National and Labour battle it out in knife-edge New Zealand poll
articles.summary: Polls show no coalition is expected to secure a majority of seats, in one of the closest elections in recent history

blocks.text: Let the count begin

Six weeks of campaigning, politicking and debates is done. New Zealand has voted and over the next few hours we’ll find out the results of what has been cast as one of the tightest elections in recent memory.

For weeks, the polls have shown no clear path to government for any potential coalition, left or right. Seemingly unimpressed by National and Labour, polls have tracked voters turning to the smaller parties, such as the centrist Opportunity party.

Tonight could see Opportunity potentially end up as kingmaker, unless that pre-election support and hype has failed to translate into votes. Stay with us as we learn the answer to that big question and others, as we keep you across the counts and results as they come in. It’s going to be an exciting night!
Key events

items: 30m agoLet the count begin

blocks.text: Michelle Duff

As the first results of the night flashed up onto the big screen, Labour party volunteer Jasmine, 22, who works in the public service and didn’t want to use her last name, stopped talking mid-sentence.

A hush fell over the room as the first poll results show the main parties neck and neck . “That’s close,” she said, exhaling. “It’s great that Opportunity is over 5%, I’m happy about that. It’s just overwhelming; this is years of work, and that’s real numbers.” She’s been working for the party since she was 16.
Cheers are going up in the room as electorate results begin to come in. About 200 party supporters are expected here tonight.
Another update here with 8% of the vote counted.
National on 31.2%, Labour 28.4%, the Greens 12.9%, Act 11.2%, NZ First 9.6%, Opportunity 5.7% and Te Pāti Māori 0.4%.
On these numbers, we would have a right bloc coalition back in power. Long way to go.
Jamie Tahana has this from the Backbencher pub in Wellington:

At the Backbencher, a politics and puppet themed pub across the road from the Beehive, people are splitting their attention between the election coverage, the football, the cricket, and tonight’s rugby league.

Many people spoken to by the Guardian weren’t prepared to go bold with a prediction, nervous about the likely tight result. One man, Joel, told the Guardian Opportunity making parliament would “shake things up.”
Also here is NZ First local candidate and former Wellington mayor Andy Foster, and his team. Foster said he was nervous.
“Let’s get through tonight, but I’m feeling confident,” he told the Guardian. “The country needs NZ First and we still have a lot to do,” he said.
Some colour from voting stations around the country today.

blocks.caption: A dog sits outside a voting place on election day in Wellington.  Photograph: Charlotte Graham-McLay/AP
Electoral officials speak to voters inside a voting place at Kokiri Marae on the day of the general election in Lower Hutt.  Photograph: Hollie Adams/Reuters
People enter a voting place at St Anne’s Anglican church on the day of the general election in Wellington. Photograph: Hollie Adams/Reuters
Election workers prepare ballot papers for voters in Wellington. Photograph: Charlotte Graham-McLay/AP

blocks.text: The Labour party election night event has kicked off in the Upper Hutt Cosmopolitan Club, a popular suburban venue in the middle of Labour party leader Chris Hipkins’ Remutaka electorate, which he’s held since 2008.

As Te Awa Kairangi (the Hutt River) flows by a few sleepy streets away, the Cossie Club has begun to fill with party supporters and volunteers, many who are travelling to this small city in the Wellington region by bus. At first stride into this red-hued room, festooned with fairy lights and balloons, it’s difficult to know if you’ve walked into a political event or a 21st party.

Politicians expected here tonight include Ginny Anderson, Labour’s candidate for the Hutt South electorate; Barbara Edmonds, standing for Mana; and Ayesha Verrall, who is contesting Wellington North against incumbent Green party MP Tamatha Paul.
Hipkins (whose nickname is Chippy) said his family tradition is fish and chips on election night as the votes are counted, so he is expected here later.

blocks.caption: Eva Corlett

blocks.text: Eva Corlett
Seats to watch
Hutt South, Nelson, Banks Peninsula, Wigram, Whanganui and Kāpiti were either tight races between National and Labour last time around, or could change hands after boundaries were re-drawn.
Wairarapa, West Coast-Tasman and Hamilton East are historically National strongholds. If they flip red, that could be an early signal for good overall outcome for Labour.

The Tāmaki electorate has traditionally been held by National but was taken by the libertarian Act party in 2023. This year, the race between those parties’ candidates and newcomer Labour candidate Max Harris is tight – a Harris win would be a surprise upset for the right.

Meanwhile, Green candidate Kahurangi Carter is vying to claim Christchurch Central. If Greens co-leader Chlöe Swarbrick keeps Auckland Central and Tamatha Paul nabs Wellington North, New Zealand’s three largest city centre electorates will be represented by the Green party.

Maungakiekie could also be an indicator for the final results. Over the past two elections, the Maungakiekie electorate has proven to be an “extraordinary” bellwether seat, accurately reflecting the mood of the nation.
If six weeks of campaigning has left you cold, then sit back as Matilda Boseley spills the tea on the two Chrises, election vibes and the Luxon-Opportunity question.

blocks.caption: What’s up with the New Zealand election? – video

blocks.text: Seeing some numbers. So with just 1% of the vote counted, National are on 31%, Labour 29.8% and Opportunity party 5.7%, so they are above the threshold. There is obviously a long, long way to go tonight. The Greens are on 12.2%, Act 11% and New Zealand First 9.4%. Te Pāti Māori are on 0.3%.

So, what’s at stake for Luxon and National tonight? A lot. The party is facing the dire possibility of being the first one-term National-led government since it was founded in 1936. Remember, National has never led for less than three terms, ever. So this is a huge night for Luxon’s legacy and the National party, both past and present.

blocks.caption: Ahead of tonight, Christopher Luxon has long struggled in the preferred prime minister poll. Photograph: Phil Walter/Getty Images

blocks.text: Tonight, our New Zealand correspondent Eva Corlett is posted at National party’s main gathering at Viaduct Events Centre, in Auckland, awaiting the arrival of Christopher Luxon.

In Upper Hutt, north of Wellington, we’ll have updates from Michelle Duff who is mingling alongside the Labour faithful at the local Cosmopolitan Club. That’s happening in Chris Hipkins’ electorate, and he’ll show up there once the lay of the electoral land becomes clear.

In Wellington, Jamie Tahana is at the Backbenchers pub, which is a brief stroll from New Zealand’s Beehive. He’ll be checking the mood with keen voters who have pulled up a pew and are ready to watch the results start coming in.

articles.title: US midterm results may help unite Israeli coalition to unseat Netanyahu
articles.summary: Democrats’ sweep could urge Israel’s divided opposition to join forces and remove prime minister closely allied with Trump

blocks.text: The Democrats’ sweep of Congress may make it easier for Israel’s splintered opposition to overcome deep internal divisions and form a coalition government, by increasing the urgency of unseating Benjamin Netanyahu, who has associated himself so closely with Donald Trump’s Republicans.
But as Israel took stock of the results, there was also a sense that the elections marked a longer-term shift in US politics that will make the job of any new Israeli leader far more difficult.

The United States provides Israel with critical military and diplomatic support, so nurturing bipartisan ties was the cornerstone of foreign policy for decades. Netanyahu ripped up that commitment to throw his lot in with the Republicans in general and Trump in particular.
The opposition had always attacked his decision as ill-judged. By the end of the week, they were warning that it was positively dangerous.

“These people aren’t against Israel,” prominent opposition politician Yair Lapid said of incoming Democratic lawmakers, urging his country to rebuild bridges. “They’re mainly against Netanyahu – for them, anything connected to him is toxic.”
“The easiest thing is to scream that ‘America is lost,’ because if it’s lost, you don’t have to work. That’s just not true. Not at all.”
Lapid laid out a plan to “rebuild trust” in the US, but it perhaps did more to demonstrate the scale of the problem than reassure Israelis.
His proposal of a transatlantic charm offensive by officials of a prospective new government drew a swift and sharp rebuke from the New York congressman-elect Brad Lander.
Lander, a Democrat who is Jewish and describes himself as a liberal Zionist, was detained in the occupied West Bank last month while joining Palestinians trying to harvest olives.

“Minister Lapid: As someone who won a seat in Congress last night, and who cares about Israel: you’re not listening to what American voters – Jewish and non-Jewish – are saying,” Lander wrote in a direct response.
“We aren’t starving for a barnstorming tour. We’re hungry to see respect for international law and human rights.”

In his exchange with Lapid, Lander also highlighted the arrest of journalist Abed Abu Shehada, a Palestinian citizen of Israel, as an example of how Israel violates international law. He drew a direct link with the ICE “regime of detention without charges, based on secret evidence, designed to intimidate and chill speech” that he said was rejected by US voters.

Abu Shehada was reportedly taken from his home by 15 masked security officials in a night-time raid, without an arrest warrant. Interrogators have only questioned him about a podcast interview with a public figure, lawyers acting for Abu Shehada said.
On Friday, Lander and two other incoming Jewish members of Congress, Daniel Bliss and Scott Wiener, wrote to Israel’s ambassador to the US calling for the immediate release of Abu Shehada.

“Detaining a reporter for conducting an interview — the only issue that interrogators questioned him about — is a violation of international law,” Lander said when he published the letter. “It comes at a time when senior Israeli officials are trying to delegitimize the participation of Palestinian citizens in Israel’s recent elections.”
Nor do Israel’s problems end with angry Democrats. The wounded Republican establishment lost no time looking a few thousand miles away to find reasons for the collapse of its voter base.

Soon after the election results came in, the vice-president, JD Vance, put “our relationship with Israel” on a short list of reasons for voter fury, and on election day Trump made a last-ditch attempt to woo voters with a pledge to cut off $4bn (£3bn) in annual military aid to Israel.

The announcement caused panic in Israel’s defence establishment. “When the commander of the Israel air force hears something like that, he might slit his wrists,” one official told Channel 12 news. “Where are we going to come up with 15 billion shekels every year, and what does that mean for Israel’s future defence budget?”

Netanyahu only responded to Trump’s electioneering on Friday with an attempt to spin the cut as a joint decision reflecting Israel’s economic strength. It demonstrated a “move from aid to partnership”, his office said in a statement.

Netanyahu has long flaunted his relationship with Trump, his fluent English and experience in the US, presenting himself as the only man with the international standing to guarantee Israel’s security in a hostile world.
After Tuesday’s US election, he looks more like an agent of its destruction to many in Israel. “One thing is clear: we are losing America,” Ben Caspit wrote in Ma’ariv, a daily newspaper.

“This isn’t a process; it isn’t happening in stages; it is happening all at once. It is an avalanche. It is a reverberating collapse of the foundation of Israel’s national defence doctrine. This isn’t a decree of fate. It is a decree of Netanyahu.”

Some advocates for change inside Israel found cause for hope in the Democrats’ victory, if Israel’s opposition can turn their mandate for change into a new government. They won 67 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, but more than a quarter went to Palestinian citizens of Israel, and some of the Jewish Israeli opposition parties have ruled out sitting with them.

US administrations have for too long equated support for Israel with blind support for its government, said Nadav Tamir, a former senior Israeli diplomat in the US who is now executive director of J Street Israel.
That consensus is cracking, but the majority of lawmakers from both parties still see Israel as a key US ally in the Middle East, he wrote in the Times of Israel.

External pressure from those who support its security but see current policy as self-destructive might push the country towards necessary change, including a resolution of the Israel-Palestine conflict.

“Perhaps this will be the paradox of the new [US] Congress,” he wrote. “It will be less willing to define support for Israel as automatic alignment with every policy of its government, but precisely for that reason, it may offer Israel more meaningful support in breaking out of the cycle of wars and building a future of security and prosperity.”

articles.title: Bigger bank, broader base: TG Limcaoco’s BPI years
articles.summary: From overseeing a bank merger to scrapping transfer fees and bringing banking into neighborhood stores, it's been a busy five years for Limcaoco

blocks.text: LAST DANCE? BPI president and CEO TG Limcaoco speaks at the bank's 175th gala on October 26, 2026.
BPI
From overseeing a bank merger to scrapping transfer fees and bringing banking into neighborhood stores, it's been a busy five years for Limcaoco

items: Jose Teodoro 'TG' Limcaoco will step down as president and CEO of the Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) in April 2027, transitioning to a senior role within the Ayala Group.

Under Limcaoco's leadership, BPI's annual net income increased significantly, and the bank expanded its customer base and services, including the introduction of free money transfers and agency banking.

Limcaoco emphasized the importance of financial inclusion and expressed concerns about the limited access to formal financial services for many Filipinos, while also engaging with the community through initiatives like a Disney-themed savings account for children.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
After five years at the helm of the 175-year-old Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI), Jose Teodoro “TG” Limcaoco is ready to say goodbye to the country’s oldest bank.

Limcaoco will step down as president and chief executive officer in April 2027, making way for consumer banking chief Maria Cristina “Ginbee” Go, BPI’s first female CEO. He will remain on the board and take on other senior roles within the Ayala Group.

Five years is a short chapter for a bank that has survived colonial governments, wars, and economic crises. But Limcaoco was hardly new to BPI or the Ayalas when he took the helm in 2021. He had been president of BPI Capital and BPI Family Savings Bank, then spent six years as Ayala Corporation’s chief financial officer.
The bank he inherited from Cezar “Bong” Consing was already one of the country’s largest. The one he will leave behind is considerably bigger.

BPI’s annual net income rose from P23.88 billion in 2021 to P66.62 billion in 2025, while assets grew from P2.42 trillion at end-2021 to P3.9 trillion by September 2026. Its customer base more than doubled to over 19 million, helped in part by the 2024 merger with Robinsons Bank.

But enough of the numbers, and back to the man of the hour. Limcaoco isn’t your typical banker who shies away from the media. He’s frank, sometimes even blunt, and always ready to break down a tough banking topic with an example or two.

Ask him about bank secrecy, and he’ll point out that few countries have laws as restrictive as the Philippines’. Ask about reserve requirements, and he’ll explain why he prefers interest rates as a monetary policy tool.
When Rappler asked last July why BPI made transfers free, he explained that under new central bank rules, it could charge only around P1.50. Why bother customers over that amount?
“You’re just needling the customer,” he said.

BPI became one of the first major commercial banks to permanently waive InstaPay and PESONet fees, with others following with cuts of their own. There was a business case, too. Free transfers could keep customers using BPI and perhaps bring in more business.

Much the same thinking has gone into the bank’s expansion into agency banking under Limcaoco. Customers can now open accounts, deposit, and withdraw money at participating supermarkets and convenience stores — often for free — while BPI avoids some of the costs of branches and ATMs.
In a March interview with McKinsey, Limcaoco summed it up: “Our philosophy is, if you cannot come to the bank, we will bring the bank to you.”
Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Deputy Governor Bernadette Romulo-Puyat, who has taken a particular interest in the program, had some rather warm words for Limcaoco.

“Ang galing ni TG (TG’s great),” she told Rappler in a recent chat about financial inclusion. “My experience with him, he was really looking for ways to help give everybody a bank account. He’s made it so simple.”

blocks.caption: [Vantage Point] The bank Ginbee Go will inherit

blocks.text: At BPI’s 175th anniversary gala in October, chairman Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala credited Limcaoco with bringing “real dynamism” to the bank, while welcoming to its next chapter under Go.
Limcaoco, meanwhile, spent much of his own speech looking beyond his time at the bank. He wondered aloud what banking might look like 25 years from now, when BPI celebrates its 200th anniversary.
“I don’t think any of us can predict exactly what banking will look like by then,” he said.
Yet he was clear on one unfinished job: “Millions of Filipinos still have limited access to formal financial services.”

blocks.caption: GALA. BPI president and CEO TG Limcaoco (right) looks on as BPI chairman Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala congratulates writer Roel Landingin. BPI

blocks.text: But Limcaoco isn’t always dressed up to the nines. A rather different side of him was on display two months earlier, on August 1, BPI’s actual birthday, when the bank launched a Disney-themed savings account for children.

After a morning of golf, Limcaoco, a grandfather himself, was at Glorietta — an Ayala mall, of course — talking to children about setting aside part of their allowance. As he often does, he brought the idea down to their level. Compound interest might mean little to a child, but saving for a bicycle or a dog was easy enough to understand.
“Maybe a kid puts P100 a month,” he told Rappler afterward. “The magic of interest, even though it’s small, really is meaningful.”

Meanwhile Go, then still a few months away from being officially announced as his successor, took the chance to tease her boss, joking during her remarks about whether the children should call him “Lolo TG.”
For that morning, at least, the man running one of the country’s biggest banks was simply Lolo TG, talking to kids about what they could do for their future. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Angara calls for stricter digital protection for students
articles.summary: Department of Education Secretary Sonny Angara urged technology and social media firms to implement tougher age-verification controls and delete online content that highlights violence and targets…

blocks.text: Published November 7, 2026 1:56pm

Department of Education Secretary Sonny Angara urged technology and social media firms to implement tougher age-verification controls and delete online content that highlights violence and targets young learners into radicalization.

"We agree that we need stronger safeguards against these terrorist recruitment groups, online groomers. We need to protect our children online, and we really need stricter firewalls, not systems where a child who isn’t even in high school can just click that they are 18 years old. That cannot be allowed,” Angara said at a multisectoral forum on preventing nihilistic violent extremism (NVE) held at the University of Asia and the Pacific (UA&P).
Angara said the call came amid President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s directive to all government agencies to seek lasting solutions to the complex issue of school violence.

Following Marcos’ orders, the Department of Education (DepEd) has created a task force with the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) and the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) child protection units to track emerging risks.

The education secretary lauded the government agencies and international and local partners for their solidarity in dealing with school safety and digital threats, adding that a number of social media companies have reached out to DepEd for discussions about enhancing safeguards in online spaces.
To combat both online and physical threats, Angara said the agency has enhanced school, learner support, and emergency response systems.
Angara said the DepEd has also partnered with the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) to deploy barangay officials to support campus security and police visibility.

"We must remember that while we actively stand guard and protect our children in the physical world, we also need to do the same online. We need to build stronger communities and better relationships with our learners," he said.
In line with the efforts, DepEd has expanded the Kaagapay Program to guide parents in protecting children online alongside promoting mental health awareness and identifying red flags on bullying.

Further, the agency underscored peer support through the My Buddy System and empowered school clubs, organizations, scouting and sports to provide learners positive spaces to participate. --VAL, GMA News

articles.title: 2 foreign fugitives nabbed over alleged links to large-scale fraud, illegal gambling ops
articles.summary: The Bureau of Immigration arrested two fugitives, a Taiwanese and a South Korean, in separate operations for their alleged involvement in large-scale fraud and illegal gambling operations.

blocks.text: Published November 7, 2026 1:51pm
The Bureau of Immigration (BI) arrested two fugitives, a Taiwanese and a South Korean, in separate operations for their alleged involvement in large-scale fraud and illegal gambling operations.

In a press release issued Saturday, the BI identified the Taiwanese fugitive as Yu Sheng Fu, 27, who was apprehended in Barangay Cabancalan, Mandaue City on October 29 following a request from the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office.

“According to Taiwan’s Criminal Investigation Bureau (CIB), Yu allegedly leads a fraud syndicate operating in Manila that victimized more than 200 Taiwanese nationals and defrauded them of over P200 million,” the BI added.

Meanwhile, South Korean Ha Jonhoo, 46, was arrested at the Newport Complex in Pasay City on November 2. He was wanted by South Korean authorities for his alleged involvement in an illegal online gambling operation.
The bureau said Ha reportedly acted as a junket agent who facilitated remote baccarat gambling for Korean clients from June 2019 to December 2020.
“The operation allegedly involved 37 transactions amounting to approximately 154 million South Korean won, or US$114,000,” the bureau added.
BI said both fugitives are presently detained at its detention facility in Taguig City, awaiting deportation proceedings.
After deportation orders are issued, the bureau said both will be blacklisted, barring their return to the Philippines.

BI Commissioner Joel Anthony Viado said these arrests show the agency’s efforts to prevent the country from becoming a refuge from justice, noting the bureau's continued vigilance to ensure observance of the law.

“These arrests demonstrate that international borders will not shield fugitives from accountability. The Bureau remains vigilant in tracking down foreign nationals wanted for serious offenses and ensuring that those who violate our immigration laws face the appropriate legal consequences,” Viado said.
“We will continue to act decisively while observing due process and the rule of law,” he added. —Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/KG, GMA News

articles.title: The week in photos: October 31 to November 6, 2026
articles.summary: A recap of news, sports, lifestyle, entertainment, and human interest images from the Philippines and around the globe

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Democrats took control of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections, making extraordinary gains deep in Republican territory with voters delivering a sharp rebuke to President Donald Trump and his agenda.

A wave of anger over Trump’s policies, particularly the US-Iran war’s role in pushing the cost of living higher, helped Democrats take the Senate, where they flipped seats in deeply Republican states for a majority of at least 54-44. Democrats also gained at least 30 seats in the House of Representatives.

Donald Trump’s party has been defeated in states where it hadn’t lost for a generation — or longer: Texas, South Carolina and Kansas. These have been red states for quite some time, but this shows the Republicans really suffered in their own heartland.
Meanwhile, Malacanang announced on November 5 that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has chosen Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda as the country’s 28th Supreme Court chief justice.

Zalameda, the third most senior among the chief justice nominees, replaces Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo who retired during the weekend. Zalameda will serve as chief justice for seven years or until August 2033, when he reaches the mandatory retirement age of 70.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: SC didn’t rule Marcos’ budget signing unconstitutional
articles.summary: The Court faulted Congress for raising the President's proposed budget, and with the decision not yet final, no formal probe has been opened

blocks.text: The Court faulted Congress for raising the President's proposed budget, and with the decision not yet final, no formal probe has been opened

items: The Supreme Court ruled that the national budgets for 2024 and 2025 were unconstitutional due to Congress adding excessive funds, not because of President Marcos's signature.
The ruling is not yet final, as the Office of the Solicitor General has filed a motion for clarification and reconsideration regarding the budget's legality.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
Claim: The Supreme Court (SC) ruled that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s signing of the national budget was unconstitutional.

Why we fact-checked this: A graphic shared by the Facebook page Makata Ng Bayan on November 1 shows an edited photo of Marcos, former chief justice Alexander Gesmundo, and Ombudsman Jesus Crispin “Boying” Remulla.

The text on the graphic reads: “Sinabi na ng Supreme Court na Unconstitutional ang Pagpirma ni Marcos sa Budget! Tungkulin ng Ombudsman, DOJ at COA mag Imbestiga, Pero bakit di nila ginawa? Mga Duwag ba sila o Mukhang Pera?”

(The Supreme Court has already said Marcos’s signing of the budget was unconstitutional! It’s the duty of the Ombudsman, Department of Justice (DOJ), and Commission on Audit (COA) to investigate, but why didn’t they? Are they cowards or money-hungry?)
At the time of writing, the post had 4,900 reactions, 1,200 comments, and 2,400 shares.
The facts: The SC did declare national budgets unconstitutional, but because of what Congress added to them, not because of the President’s signature.

In a ruling released on October 20, written by Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen, the Court voted 13-2 to strike down the 2024 and 2025 national budgets, along with two rules in this year’s budget on how standby funds can be released.

The Court said Congress is not allowed to make the budget bigger than what the President proposed. In 2024, lawmakers added P449.5 billion in standby funds to the budget, and P17.99 billion more for the 2025 DPWH Special Road Fund. (READ: 5 practical effects of SC ruling on unprogrammed appropriations)
Not yet final: Court spokesperson Camille Ting said the ruling is not yet final, and the Office of the Solicitor General (OSG) could file a motion for reconsideration within 15 days from notice.

The OSG has since filed a motion for clarification and partial reconsideration, signed by Solicitor General Darlene Berberabe. The motion asks the Court to spell out which projects already funded under the budgets can continue, and to declare that the 2025 Special Road Fund increase was constitutional.

It also asked the Court not to count standby funds under the same spending limit as the rest of the budget, and to treat its new rules on releasing those funds as guidance rather than binding requirements.
No ongoing investigations: As of writing, the Ombudsman, DOJ, and COA have not opened a formal probe. The Ombudsman is also waiting for the SC’s final decision.
In 2025, it temporarily put on hold a graft complaint against House leaders over the 2025 budget until the Court resolved the constitutional question with finality.

The Court said officials behind the budget increases could still face criminal, civil, or administrative cases, unless the proper court or body finds they acted in good faith. On October 26, Remulla announced a “budget watch” and said he would form a team to study the decision and determine who may be held liable.

Vice President Sara Duterte said Marcos and Congress should answer for approving the budgets, while Malacañang said it disagreed with parts of the ruling. Senator Panfilo Lacson and Representative Leila de Lima welcomed the decision as a win for accountability. – Jake Gomez/Rappler.com
